title: Project Orbit: Hosted inference surface PRD, acceptance catalog, and cutover plan
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Project Orbit is a product-led PRD to unify the hosted inference surface for chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank into a single behavioral contract and prepare a staged cutover for public launch. This document captures intended behavior, non-functional SLOs, backward compatibility rules, required telemetry, QA and rollout steps, and a checklist for production readiness. Goals: 1) Provide clear, testable behavioral guarantees across generation and embedding endpoints (response format, deterministic fields, error semantics). 2) Ensure performance (p99 latency) and cost profiles meet the hosted SLA lanes. 3) Provide a validated canary cutover plan that minimizes customer-visible regressions. 4) Ship observability and rollback primitives required for safe operation. Background: Multiple product PRDs and engineering tickets have separately incremented the hosted surface (chat, multi-endpoint bundles, endpoint contracts). Orbit consolidates behavioral decisions, acceptance tests, and the cutover runbook to avoid last-mile regressions at launch. Scope (in): - API behavioral contract for hosted chat/completions/embeddings/rerank: JSON field definitions, streaming semantics, function/tool-calling signals, error codes and retries. - Acceptance test harness (simulated workloads, golden prompt sets, quality monitoring). - Performance SLOs and load profiles for 3 hosted tiers (dev, standard, enterprise). - Canary and regional cutover plan with rollback thresholds. - Console dashboard pages for per-route latency/cost and quality regression alerts. Scope (out): - Dedicated customer-side on-prem packaging. - New model onboarding beyond the curated catalog for the launch. - Deep integration with vendor-specific KMS beyond baseline KMS integration. Behavioral guarantees: - Outputs must conform to the response schema (top-level 'data' with 'type', 'attributes', and 'meta') for all endpoints. - Streaming partials permitted only for generation endpoints; when streaming is enabled, the final message must still validate against the schema. - Deterministic housekeeping fields: request_id, model_version, route_version. - Failure modes: transient infra errors mapped to 429/503 with standardized retry-after semantics; user input validation failures use 400-series. Performance & reliability targets: - Dev tier: p95 < 450ms, p99 < 850ms for short prompts (<= 256 tokens). - Standard tier: p95 < 220ms, p99 < 400ms. - Enterprise tier (reserved): p95 < 120ms, p99 < 220ms. - Availability target for hosted lanes: 99.95% monthly. Data and privacy: - No customer prompts or outputs are used for model training; retention policy for logs is 30 days unless customer opts in. - KMS integration required for enterprise lanes and validated prior to canary launch. Metrics & telemetry: - Token-level cost and latency, per-model and per-route breakdowns, error-class distributions, quality regression signal (BLEU/embedding-distance/LLM evals) for key prompt sets. - Build a health score that combines p99 latency, error budget consumption, and quality regression; used in automated cutover decision. Migration & compatibility: - The new route_version header will be added; older route_version values must continue to be accepted for 90 days with deprecation warnings. - Strict schema mode will be opt-in for 30 days post-launch; default stays permissive to avoid breaking live clients. Operational playbook summary: - Canary progressive ramp: 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 72 hours, gated by health score checks every 30min. - Automated rollback triggers: p99 increases by >40% vs baseline OR error-rate increase >200% OR quality-score degradation >5% on golden prompts. - Postmortem and hotfix runbook linked in links. Acceptance test harness: - Golden prompt set of 600 prompts distributed across domains (customer service, code, math, summarization, embeddings for semantic search). - Automated evaluation: quality delta thresholds per domain; performance under synthetic spike traffic (2x expected peak) and sustained load.
acceptance_criteria: API contract validated: all endpoints return the documented schema in 100% of sample tests (5000 synthetic calls)
Behavioral stability: quality regression on golden prompt set < 1.5% aggregated and < 5% per-domain at canary stages
Performance: hosted standard tier meets p99 <= 400ms on synthetic canary load (95% of runs)
Observability: Console has per-route latency/cost charts, error breakdown, and the quality regression alert with runbook links
Security: KMS integration validated on enterprise lane, and security review completed with sign-off
Canary gating: automated health-score checks and rollback automation are operational and tested in staging
Docs: Public API docs and SDK samples updated; deprecation notices added for route_version lifecycle
Migration: Backward compatibility test passing for legacy clients with route_version header for 90-day window
checklist: Finalize PRD and sign-off from product, engineering, design, and security
Lock API schema and publish OpenAPI / JSON schema artifacts
Implement acceptance test harness and run full golden-prompt suite in staging
Run scaled performance tests (1x, 2x expected peak) and document cost-per-token impact
Wire telemetry: per-token latency, model-version tagging, error-class and quality metrics to monitoring
Prepare console dashboards and alarm thresholds; attach runbook links
KMS validation on enterprise lane and security post-review checklist
Create canary routing configuration and automated rollback playbook in infra repo
Draft public docs, SDK examples, and changelog entry with migration guidance
Legal & privacy sign-off on telemetry retention and logging defaults
Coordinate support training and internal runbook distribution
Schedule cutover window and calendar invites with on-call and responsible engineers
Execute staged canary ramp and monitor gates; escalate per runbook if thresholds breached
Run post-cutover evaluation and publish launch report and action items
